newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Timor meeting aimed at hurting relations - Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Timor meeting aimed at hurting relations - Mahathir.

text.p: A conference on East Timor in Malaysia earlier this month was aimed at damaging Malaysia's relations with Indonesia, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad was quoted as saying.

Asia Business News (ABN) said on Tuesday that in an ABN interview Mahathir had dismissed criticism that his supporters and police acted too harshly during the conference, which came to an early end on November 9.
Mahathir was quoted in an ABN statement as saying of those attending the conference: "They came to Malaysia to have this meeting purely to make our relations with Indonesia bad.

"Malaysia is not crucial. So we told them you can have your meeting elsewhere but not in Malaysia because we have good relations with Indonesia," Mahathir was quoted as saying in the interview, due to be broadcast on Tuesday.

The meeting, the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor II, was scheduled to run three days but was disrupted when about 100 members of a group called the People's Action Front entered the meeting site and stormed the conference.

Later more than 100 people, including conference participants and journalists, as well as some of those who disrupted the meeting, were detained by police. Malaysia subsequently deported 46 foreign participants.
The Malaysian government had opposed the conference, fearing it would harm ties with neighbouring Indonesia, which invaded East Timor in 1975 and rules it in defiance of the United Nations.
